notes: Iterative problems, in the SlopCodeBench sense: the model extends ITS OWN prior answer under a spec that grows. asks accumulate across checkpoints, so coverage stays comparable. budget grows with the spec, so growth is not automatically a defect.

checkpoints.spec: Write an email telling a customer their scheduled data migration slipped by two weeks.
The customer also asked what happens to their existing data during the delay, and whether they are billed for the extra two weeks. Cover both.
asks: says what happens to existing data

checkpoints.spec: Legal now requires the email to state the one action the customer must take before the new date, and a contact for questions.
asks: names the one required customer action

checkpoints.spec: Support says two other customers read the last version as 'the data is gone'. Make it impossible to read that way, and say what will not change.
Explain why our read-through cache is returning stale prices.
Also cover how to verify the fix worked in production, and what metric would catch a regression.
asks: says how to verify in production

checkpoints.spec: The same document must now serve on-call. Add what to do at 3am when it happens again.
Add the tradeoff we accepted and the one case where the fix does not hold.
asks: names the case where the fix fails

checkpoints.spec: Write a short lesson script that teaches grade 2 students to identify 2D shapes.
asks: a hook a 7 year old likes

checkpoints.spec: Add properties of each shape, at grade 2 level.
Add real-life examples the kids can point at, and two practice exercises.
The teacher has 5 minutes of video, not 10. Keep everything above and make it fit.
asks: still covers all of the above
